guitar.definition: A stringed instrument usually having six strings.

violin.definition: Bowed stringed instrument that is the highest member of the violin family.
violin.exampleUsage: The violin rests near the player’s shoulder.

cello.exampleUsage: The seated musician supports the cello upright.
cello.definition: A large bowed string instrument usually played upright by a seated musician.

bass.definition: A bass guitar providing low notes in this lesson; bass has other instrumental and vocal senses.
bass.exampleUsage: The bass guitar provides low notes.

harp.definition: A large string instrument played by plucking its strings.

ukulele.definition: A small plucked string instrument usually having four strings.

banjo.definition: A stringed instrument of the guitar family that has long neck and circular body.
banjo.exampleUsage: The banjo has a circular body.

mandolin.definition: A stringed instrument related to the lute, usually played with a plectrum.
mandolin.exampleUsage: Omar asks about the paired strings on the mandolin.

viola.definition: A bowed string instrument, larger and lower-pitched than a violin.

double-bass.definition: The largest and lowest-pitched common member of the orchestral string family, played upright.
double-bass.exampleUsage: The double bass played the lowest notes in the ensemble.

flute.definition: A woodwind instrument usually producing sound from air directed across an opening.
flute.exampleUsage: Maya directs air across the concert flute’s opening.

clarinet.definition: A single-reed instrument with a straight tube.
clarinet.exampleUsage: The clarinet uses a single reed.

saxophone.definition: A single-reed woodwind with a conical bore.

trumpet.definition: A brass instrument usually played using three valves to change notes.
trumpet.exampleUsage: The player presses a trumpet valve.

trombone.definition: A brass instrument consisting of a long tube whose length can be varied by a U-shaped slide.
trombone.exampleUsage: The trombone player moves its slide.

oboe.exampleUsage: The oboe uses a double reed.

bassoon.definition: A long, low-pitched woodwind instrument played with a double reed.

tuba.definition: A large brass instrument with a low usual range.
tuba.exampleUsage: The tuba provides low brass notes.

harmonica.definition: A small rectangular free-reed instrument having a row of free reeds set back in air holes and played by blowing into the desired hole.
harmonica.exampleUsage: Omar holds the harmonica near his mouth.

recorder.definition: A woodwind instrument blown through a mouthpiece and played using finger holes.

drums.definition: Percussion instruments played by striking stretched surfaces.

snare-drum.definition: A shallow drum has tightly stretched heads and wires held against the lower head. Striking it produces a sharp, rattling sound.
snare-drum.exampleUsage: The snare drum’s wires give a rattling quality.

bass-drum.definition: A large percussion instrument with two heads produces a deep, indefinite-pitched sound.
bass-drum.exampleUsage: The bass drum adds a deep sound.

cymbal.definition: A percussion instrument consisting of a concave brass disk.

tambourine.definition: A percussion frame with metal jingles, sometimes also having a drumhead.

xylophone.definition: A percussion instrument with wooden bars tuned to produce a chromatic scale and with resonators.
xylophone.exampleUsage: Mallets strike the xylophone’s wooden bars.

triangle.definition: A metal percussion instrument shaped as a triangle and struck with a metal beater.

bongo.definition: A small hand drum usually played as part of a pair.

gong.definition: A metal percussion instrument struck to make a deep ringing sound.

piano.definition: A keyboard instrument whose keys cause hammers to strike strings.

keyboard.definition: A musical instrument with keys, often producing sound electronically.

organ.definition: A keyboard instrument that produces sustained sound through pipes or electronic sound generation.

synthesizer.definition: (music) an electronic instrument (usually played with a keyboard) that generates and modifies sounds electronically and can imitate a variety of other musical instruments.
synthesizer.exampleUsage: Omar changes a sound on the synthesizer.

accordion.exampleUsage: The accordion player moves the bellows.

melody.definition: A succession of notes forming a distinctive sequence.

rhythm.definition: The pattern of musical sounds and silences over time.

tempo.definition: (music) the speed at which a composition is to be played.

beat.definition: A regular pulse in a piece of music.

note.definition: A musical sound or the written symbol representing it.

rest.definition: A written musical symbol indicating a period of silence.

scale.definition: A sequence of musical notes arranged in ascending or descending pitch.

key.definition: A lever pressed to produce or control a note on an instrument.

pitch.definition: How high or low a musical sound is.

harmony.definition: The structure of music with respect to the composition and progression of chords.

dynamics.definition: The loudness or softness of music and changes in that level.

music-stand.definition: A lightweight support keeps pages of written music open and visible while someone plays.

sheet-music.definition: A visual record of a musical work shows performers its notes, rhythms, volume changes, and other instructions.

metronome.definition: A mechanical or electronic device producing a regular pulse for timing.

tuner.definition: A device or tool used to check the pitch of an instrument.

amplifier.definition: A device that makes an audio signal stronger.
amplifier.exampleUsage: The amplifier strengthens the microphone’s signal.

microphone.definition: A device that changes sound into an electrical recording or signal.
microphone.exampleUsage: The microphone converts the singer’s sound into a signal.

speaker.definition: A box that plays sound out loud into the room.

headphones.definition: A listening device worn over or close to the ears.

conductor's-baton.definition: A thin stick used by an orchestra or choir conductor to make musical gestures visible to performers.
conductor's-baton.exampleUsage: The conductor raised the baton before the music began.

music-book.definition: A book containing printed music, songs, exercises, or information for musicians.
music-book.exampleUsage: The student opened the music book to the next piece.
